VBO:0200890.summary: Friendly, confident dogs that readily engage with people are the Goldendoodle association’s breeding aim for every size. The Miniature Goldendoodle is a smaller Golden Retriever–Poodle companion cross. Active play is part of the standard’s picture, alongside a light, flowing trotting gait.
VBO:0200890.shortDescription: A smaller Golden Retriever–Poodle companion cross, bred toward friendly confidence and an active, playful character.

sources.title: GANA — Goldendoodle Breed Standard, explicit Mini size division
sources.evidence: Friendly/confident/engaging/welcoming character and companionship are selection aims, Golden Retriever and Poodle only founding breeds with founding or multigenerational stock permitted, active play and light flowing trotting gait. Mini height strictly over14 and under17in is determining size, typically26–35lb. No child/service/therapy/health/allergy claims adopted.

VBO:0201426.summary: Lively, alert and quietly confident in the breed standard, the Wire-Haired Jack Russell shares the working character of the breed’s other coat varieties. Its ancestors ran with foxhounds and went below ground to flush quarry. John Russell developed that terrier strain in England in the nineteenth century.
VBO:0201426.shortDescription: An alert, quietly confident rough-coated Jack Russell, with a history of following foxhounds and flushing quarry.

sources.title: FCI Standard345 — Jack Russell Terrier, three coat varieties
sources.evidence: Lively/alert/active, friendly and quietly confident normative character; working to ground, strain developed by Reverend John Russell in1800s England to follow foxhounds and bolt quarry. Explicit rough/broken/smooth and rectangular shorter JRT vs taller square Parson. Rough weatherproof coat must not be stripped to appear other coat.25–30cm, optional docking allows selected full natural tail at rest.

sources.title: Royal Kennel Club — current Jack Russell Terrier standard
sources.evidence: Bold/friendly/confident, developed by John Russell from fox-terrier strain in1800s to follow foxhounds and bolt quarry. Explicit three coats and separate taller Parson history. Literal rectangular25–30cm adult, dark almond eyes/button or drop ears/strong real muzzle/normal functional limbs; high-set balanced tail may drop at rest, no numeric undocked length asserted.
